text:
paul: odd bug reported by partner: in their corp VPN + mobile browser, our JS sampleapp JSON parser throws. they captured the eventstream and it looks like two JSON objects got glued together with no newline between data frames after a reconnect. anyone seen "glued" frames before?

emma: glued as in `}{` between JSON objects? can you paste the raw capture?

paul: yup, snippet from their tcpdump: 

 data: {"cid":"a1","txt":"hello"}
  data: {"cid":"a2","txt":"world"}
  data: {"cid":"a3","txt":"!"}

but because of a TLS record boundary/packet coalescing through their VPN the capture showed this arriving as: 

 data: {"cid":"a1","txt":"hello"}
data: {"cid":"a2","txt":"world"}
data: {"cid":"a3","txt":"!"}

and in another capture the service worker combined flushes and we saw `}
data: {` replaced by `}{"cid"` causing the SDK's naive "read whole buffer then JSON.parse" to choke because it tried to parse `{"cid":"a2","txt":"world"}{"cid":"a3"...` as one JSON object.

zack: whoa. that's a different class of corruption than post-DONE late chunks. here it's boundary collapse during TLS coalescing in the VPN/proxy stack.

tyler: quick question: does the JS sampleapp currently assume each `data:` line maps 1:1 to a JSON object? if so that's brittle. we should always parse per data-line and never attempt to JSON.parse a concatenation of multiple lines.

paul: sampleapp does per-line in some places but our older parsing path in the onboarding code tried to JSON.parse the entire buffer for performance. that exact optimization caused the crash. partner hit it because their network stack removed the newline boundary between frames.

emma: mitigation plan: 1) immediate: change sampleapp onboarding code to split on `
data:` and parse each data chunk independently, ignoring empty fragments; add unit tests simulating glued frames. 2) cross-SDK: add a robust reassembly utility that treats `data:` tokens as separators and tolerates missing newlines. 3) telemetry: emit sdk.stream.parse_error_glue when we detect concatenated JSON parse attempts so infra can quantify.

zack: agree. also add a small defensive fallback: if parse of a chunk fails but it looks like `}{` inside, try to heuristically split on `}{` and parse pieces. it's hacky but helps avoid crashes in the wild. mark it experimental and opt-in via config.

tyler: infra action: can you file a ticket to check whether our dev onboarding hosts or any public proxies compress/alter SSE boundaries? if dev/prod differ we might be surfacing this only to partners with odd VPNs.

paul: created a quick PR that swaps the "whole-buffer parse" for per-line parsing in the JS sampleapp and adds a test that simulates glueing frames. it prevented the crash locally. opening cross-SDK task next.

qa-bot: Ticket created: DEVEX-998 - "SSE parsing: handle glued JSON frames from VPN/TLS coalescing; split-per-data-line + heuristic fallback" (reporter: paul)

emma: cross-SDK task details: implement a lightweight reassembler that: always splits on the `data:` prefix, trims and ignores empty lines, parses each line individually, keeps optional LRU dedupe by `cid` if present, and exposes a config flag `strictParsing` default false. add unit/integration tests that simulate glued frames, missing newlines, and post-DONE stray fragments.

zack: also add sampleapp README note: "If you use VPNs/service-workers/mobile webviews that may coalesce TLS records, you might see parser errors in older SDK versions. Upgrade to >=vX.Y which implements per-line resilient parsing."

tyler: infra: INFRA ticket created to audit onboarding hosts and public proxy headers. we'll follow up if dev hosts are doing extra compression or chunk coalescing.

paul: thanks all. this one was subtle but the per-line reassembler + small heuristics solves it and keeps onboarding smooth without forcing server changes. will open PRs for python/go after JS lands.

emma: nice job catching the VPN/TLS angle. makes sense to keep SDKs defensive here.
